title: Honeywell Home HL-1 — Wi-Fi setup failed
shortDescription: T9/T10 Wi-Fi thermostat failed to join the local network during onboarding.
fullDescription:
HL-1 appears during initial setup when the thermostat cannot complete the Wi-Fi handshake. Honeywell Home devices use 2.4GHz 802.11 b/g/n. Password typos, 5GHz-only SSIDs, WPA3 security, and hidden networks are the top causes.

Confirm the network broadcasts 2.4GHz and is set to WPA2. Retry setup within 10 ft of the router to rule out range problems.

fixSteps.title: Separate 2.4GHz SSID
fixSteps.instruction: Create a 2.4GHz-only SSID on your router for setup.

fixSteps.title: Retry setup near router
fixSteps.instruction: Use the Resideo/Honeywell Home app within 10 ft of the router.

whenToCallPro: If router changes are needed but unfamiliar, contact ISP.
videoSearchQuery: Honeywell Home HL-1 Wi-Fi error fix

title: Honeywell Home HL-2 — Wi-Fi lost
shortDescription: Thermostat was connected but dropped off the network.
fullDescription: HL-2 is shown when a previously connected device loses its Wi-Fi link. Usually the result of a router reboot, password change, or ISP outage.
videoSearchQuery: Honeywell Home HL-2 Wi-Fi lost fix

title: Honeywell Home HL-3 — server unreachable
shortDescription: Wi-Fi OK but cannot reach Resideo cloud.
fullDescription: Wi-Fi is present but DNS or upstream path to the Resideo cloud is broken. Check DNS settings, Resideo status, and firewall rules that may block outbound HTTPS.

title: Honeywell Home HL-4 — account not linked
shortDescription: Thermostat not associated with a Resideo account.
fullDescription: HL-4 means the device is unclaimed or was removed from an account. Complete setup in the Resideo app to bind it.

title: Honeywell Home HL-5 — firmware update failure
shortDescription: OTA firmware update did not complete.
fullDescription: HL-5 appears when the firmware download or install step fails. Wait 24h for automatic retry. Weak Wi-Fi is the most frequent cause.

fixSteps.title: Improve Wi-Fi
fixSteps.instruction: Move router closer or add mesh node.

fixSteps.title: Reboot thermostat
fixSteps.instruction: Pull breaker or remove from base briefly.

title: Honeywell Home HL-6 — sensor pairing failed
shortDescription: Smart Room Sensor will not pair with T9/T10.
fullDescription: The Smart Room Sensor uses a 915MHz mesh. Pairing issues usually trace to a dead CR2450 battery or the sensor being too far from the thermostat during the first handshake.

fixSteps.title: Pair within 3 ft
fixSteps.instruction: Hold sensor near thermostat during Add Sensor flow.

videoSearchQuery: Honeywell T9 T10 sensor pairing fix

title: Honeywell Home HL-7 — screen lockout active
shortDescription: Thermostat screen is locked via access code or app setting.
fullDescription: HL-7 indicates active screen lockout. Remove the lock via the Resideo app under device settings, or enter the 4-digit code if locally configured.

fixSteps.title: Disable in app
fixSteps.instruction: Resideo app > Settings > Screen Lock off.

fixSteps.title: Factory reset
fixSteps.instruction: If PIN is lost, factory reset via pro menu.

title: Honeywell Home HL-8 — thermostat lockout (installer)
fullDescription: HL-8 represents an installer-level lockout commonly applied by HVAC contractors. Contact your installer or use the local keypad override documented in the installer guide.

fixSteps.title: Contact installer
fixSteps.instruction: Ask your HVAC contractor for the unlock code.

title: Honeywell Home HL-9 — C-wire not detected
shortDescription: Thermostat does not see C-wire voltage.
fullDescription: T9/T10 require a C-wire for reliable operation. HL-9 indicates no C-wire detected. Install a C-wire, a dedicated C-wire adapter, or use Honeywell's THP9045 power adapter for systems without a common wire.

fixSteps.title: Install C-wire adapter
fixSteps.instruction: Use THP9045 or run dedicated C-wire.

whenToCallPro: If not comfortable at HVAC control board.
videoSearchQuery: Honeywell T10 C-wire adapter THP9045 install

title: Honeywell Home HL-10 — HVAC wiring detection error
shortDescription: Thermostat detected a wiring combination it cannot validate.
fullDescription: HL-10 occurs during wiring detection when the thermostat sees incompatible combinations (e.g., O/B set incorrectly or W2 without W1). Review equipment type in setup.

causes.cause: Incorrect O/B set in equipment menu

title: Honeywell Home reading differs from actual temperature
fullDescription: Usually caused by mounting location (sun, vent, exterior wall). Apply a correction offset under Preferences > Temperature Display.

title: Honeywell Home connection issue (app can't control)
shortDescription: App cannot send commands even though thermostat shows online.
fullDescription: Commands time out despite thermostat reporting online. This is usually a stale session — sign out of the Resideo app and sign back in. If persistent, remove and re-add the device.

fixSteps.title: Sign out/in
fixSteps.instruction: Resideo app > Settings > Sign Out then sign in again.

fixSteps.title: Remove/re-add
fixSteps.instruction: If unresolved, remove device and re-add.
